source.stream_facts_verified: Video: av1 (libdav1d) Main, yuv420p(tv, bt709), 1280x720, 30 fps, 30 tbr, 16k tbn; container Duration 00:02:53.65; audio aac 48kHz stereo (not used). Title/duration/fps from source.json are metadata claims, not stream facts; stream facts above read from ffmpeg -i of the retained bytes.

screening.range: 0-45 s only, 2 fps sparse index (90 frames, r5atmp/screen/s-001..s-090, sheet.jpg)
screening.classification: 0-45 s is a continuous shot of a kinetic lyric typography sequence: flat cyan background, monochrome Miku-style girl with yellow hat (static pose), Japanese lyric glyphs entering with scale pops and single-frame appearances. No player UI, watermark, progress bar or scene cut observed in the 90 screening frames. All text is in-frame lyric typography, not UI.
screening.candidates: A: 17.0-19.5 s (glyph scale pop + sequential entries); B: 32.0-34.5 s (fade-in entry). A selected for richer same-glyph size trajectory plus two in-window text changes.

window_decode.command: ffmpeg -nostdin -hide_banner -v info -i media/BV1J8hf61EAt/source.mp4 -vf "select='between(n,519,554)',showinfo" -fps_mode passthrough -an -f image2 r5atmp/window/w-%03d.png (plus identical select to raw yuv420p for hashing)
window_decode.note: framehash filter absent in this build ('No such filter: framehash'); decoded-frame hashes computed as MD5 of raw yuv420p bytes per frame (1280x720, 1036800 bytes each) from a single rawvideo decode

observations_frame_grounded.read_method: full-resolution reads: 2fps sheet (256px) for screening only; native 30fps 200px sheets for candidate choice; 400px full-resolution transition strips (n517-525, n539-556, r5atmp/window/transitions.jpg) and 960px single frames for glyph claims. Low-resolution sheet reads produced a mislabel (large glyph initially read as 'また'; full resolution shows '気') - full resolution is authoritative.
observations_frame_grounded.composition: single continuous shot, no cut; flat cyan background with soft darker vertical bands at frame edges; monochrome Miku-style girl (yellow knit hat, twin tails) centered, upper-body, pose static across all 36 frames (no visible character motion)
observations_frame_grounded.left_vertical_column: vertical lyric column at the left edge (small, black serif) present across the window; small warm-red accent marks (dot/dash) above column glyphs visible from n523

main_glyph_ki.glyph: 気 (large, upper-left, overlapping the hat region)
main_glyph_ki.size_trajectory: grows from ~60% of final size at n519 (17.300s) to full size at n523 (17.433s); position fixed (no visible translation); same-glyph scale-up over ~5 frames; no intermediate opacity frames observed; mechanism (scale keyframe vs asset swap vs re-render) not inferable from appearance
main_glyph_ki.exit: outside window: shrinking begins at n555 (18.500s, neighbor frame)
main_glyph_ki.anatomy_observed: black solid fill, no outline; wedge/serif terminals at stroke ends; clear thick-horizontal/thin-vertical stroke contrast; angular joints. (Family label such as Song/Ming is interpretation, not a visible fact.)

right_glyph_entries.な: absent at n524, fully present at n525 (17.467s) at fixed position and final small size - hard single-frame appearance (fade/sub-frame ramp not resolvable at 30fps)
right_glyph_entries.く: absent at n539, present at n540 (18.200s)
right_glyph_entries.て: absent at n539, present at n540 (18.200s)
right_glyph_entries.grouping: 気 (large) + な・く・て (small, sequential, right of 気) - within-window text changes: 2 (n525, n540)

observations_frame_grounded.occlusion: glyphs are the top layer over the character (気 overlaps hat; left column overlaps twin-tail edge); character midground; background flat. No rounded foreground objects in this window (unlike BV1zrbCzLEH4 window).
observations_frame_grounded.anchoring: screen-space: glyphs fixed to frame layout; character static so object-anchoring not testable; no parallax
observations_frame_grounded.conditional_applicability: the on-screen fragments read as '気' + 'なくて' (plus the left column); lyric-meaning/emotional fit is conditional on audio/lyric context and NOT verified here; no full-lyric transcription attempted per order

intermediate.build: libx264 crf12, -fps_mode passthrough, -enc_time_base filter, -video_track_timescale 16000, select n519..554, setpts=PTS-STARTPTS, no fps filter, no output -r

clip.decode_verification: 36/36 frames; integer clip pts equal to source relative pts at every index [0,533,1067,...,18667]; strictly increasing
clip.visual_correspondence: first/middle/last per-pair grayscale MAD 0.3379/0.3617/0.3970 (255 scale), max diff 8/15/11; lossy CRF12 re-encode (AV1 decode -> x264), pixel equality NOT claimed

receipt.source_pts_independently_observed: 36 absolute source pts read from fresh showinfo of the source (not copied from any prior artifact)

offline_validation.validate_native_receipt: pass on the exact final bytes + receipt
offline_validation.negative_control_1: receipt copy with last source_pts +16 ticks -> rejected native_receipt_invalid
offline_validation.negative_control_2: receipt copy with zeroed clip_sha256 -> rejected native_receipt_invalid

failed_attempts: MKV intermediate (order-mandated form) cannot preserve relative native PTS with this toolchain: matroska muxer quantizes to integer ms (no timebase AVOptions in ffmpeg 7.0.2-static, verified via -h muxer=matroska); measured decoded MKV pts grid 0,33,67,...,1167 ms collapses the 533/534-tick cadence (drift up to ~240 ticks at frame 18). Preserved: r5atmp/failed-mkv/intermediate-mkv-ms-quantized.mkv + decode-pts.txt. Substituted MP4 intermediate (same CRF12 encode) which preserves exact 1/16000 ticks, then stream-copy remux to final MP4 - the R3c MKV path only preserved cadence because that source's 528/544-tick gaps were integer ms.
framehash filter unavailable in this ffmpeg build; raw-yuv MD5 per frame used instead
later_video_prompt_proposal: PROPOSAL ONLY (not an applied client modification): the video prompt for this window must explicitly request: (1) frame-indexed entrances/exits per glyph with native frame numbers; (2) for the large glyph, same-glyph size trajectory across frames (start/mid/end size) separately from the different-glyph size hierarchy (large main vs small trailing glyphs); (3) rounded or other foreground objects ONLY if occlusion-order evidence exists in the frames (state which layer is in front); (4) glyph grouping and sequential append behavior; (5) custom stroke/outline anatomy described as observed wedge terminals and weight contrast without an unsourced font-family label; (6) screen-space vs scene-space anchoring; (7) explicit uncertainty fields for unresolvable mechanisms (fade vs hard appearance, scale keyframe vs asset swap, accent-mark purpose).
